messages.subject: 3-option probabilistic reversal learning
parts:
Hello Nate and Young,

I'm working with a 3-option probabilistic reversal learning task in which the reward probabilities are not complementary (i.e., they do not add up to 100%, so subjects cannot necessarily infer the probability of one option from feedback on the others). Is there a way to adapt the 2-option reversal learning models to fit such a task, or would you perhaps recommend the 3 armed bandit model posted earlier in this group?

Thank you for your time!

Best,
Erin

messages.author: 47d1400f432367d7
messages.subject: Re: 3-option probabilistic reversal learning
parts:
Hi Erin,


Thanks for your interest! 


It would probably be best to start off with a model like the 3-armed bandit that was posted on the forum earlier, and then you could work your way up to trying more complex models that have a reversal learning component. One model that may be useful in your case would be a 3-armed bandit with a pearce hall rule. The pearce hall rule tends to capture reversal learning pretty well. We do not have this model in hBayesDM at the moment, but here is an example application if you are interested in implementing it yourself: http://cosanlab.com/static/papers/Taylor_2017_Pain.pdf


I hope this helps! Let us know if you have any other questions.


Best,

Nate
